purpose: offline reference for the browser-side comet propagator: a local two-body propagation of the SBDB elements plus a JPL EM Bary position must reproduce these Horizons rows, with no network access at test time
frame: geocentric astrometric ICRF/J2000 RA/Dec, degrees; r and delta in au
time_scale: sample instants are UTC; add 69.184 s (TT-UTC in 2026) before treating a time as the TDB the elements are referred to

earth_model.model: JPL/Standish approximate positions, Table 1, EM Barycenter
earth_model.stated_accuracy: 20 arcsec longitude, 8 arcsec latitude, 6000 km distance over 1800-2050
earth_model.note: values at J2000 and per century, referred to the mean ecliptic and equinox of J2000

sbdb_rows.note: the rows of the single SBDB comet query that fell inside the candidate freshness window, verbatim (values as returned, still strings); this is the row set candidate selection ran on

cross_check.note: these (comet, instant) pairs appear in both this fixture and the published ephemerides artifact and must agree within the tolerance above; if the artifact is refreshed with a different horizon, re-run --build-fixture to re-align

propagator_check.model: two-body Kepler propagation of the SBDB elements (elliptical/parabolic/hyperbolic) + JPL/Standish EM Bary position, J2000 ecliptic -> equatorial
propagator_check.note: measured error of the model the browser propagator repeats; it grows with the time from the element epoch because this model has no non-gravitational acceleration and no planetary perturbations

notes: 2P: one sample is aligned with the last sample of data/overhead/comet-ephemerides.json so the two artifacts can be cross-checked at an identical instant
cobs_samples are the raw obs_list.api payloads for one published comet, fetched with the same parameters as the build so the browser test can re-derive its measured block: 2P (V, C)
sample dates are offsets from each comet's own SBDB element epoch, so the fixture keeps its meaning when JPL republishes an unrelated orbit
each comet has at least one sample within 200 days of its element epoch and one 300-800 days away
propagator_check records what this build measured for the propagation contract on the exact numbers in this file; tests/overhead-comets-data.cjs recomputes it independently
